rounds.text: Mayur Leather Products Ltd exhibits significant valuation risk, trading at a P/E ratio of 233x and a P/B ratio of 5.41x, both of which substantially exceed their respective sector benchmarks [E1, E2, E6, E7]. Operational efficiency remains a major point of contention, as the company’s ROCE of 0.81% significantly trails the sector benchmark of 10.28% [E10]. Furthermore, the company faces leverage risk with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.28x, and its cash flow profile is unstable, evidenced by negative operating cash flow of Rs -0.57 Cr in March 2026 [E29, E31]. While the stock has seen recent price appreciation, this growth has outpaced fundamental profit growth, suggesting that market expectations may be detached from the underlying financial reality [E41, E42]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong recent profit growth, including a 75% increase over the trailing twelve months, and a DCF analysis suggests the current price remains slightly below intrinsic value [E17, E38, E50].
